Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (group-based CV workflows), pain points (current workarounds), and acceptance criteria (groups parameter propagation, backward compatibility) for the SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter requirement. Questions probe workflow context, user impact, ideal behavior, and prioritization to ground requirements in end-user needs.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (group-based CV support), pain points (current API limitation), and acceptance criteria (correct groups propagation through internal call chain). Questions decompose the requirement into workflow context, stakeholder impact, technical semantics, validation approach, and edge case handling.

End-user requires SequentialFeatureSelector to support group-based cross-validation via a groups parameter in fit() to prevent data leakage in grouped/hierarchical datasets and maintain consistency with scikit-learn's standard cross-validation API.

End-users require SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() to accept a groups parameter for group-aware cross-validation, enabling proper feature selection on grouped/hierarchical data (clinical trials, time series, multi-subject studies) while maintaining scikit-learn API consistency and preventing data leakage.

End-user requires SequentialFeatureSelector to support groups parameter in fit() for grouped/hierarchical data validation. Current limitation forces custom workarounds, introduces data leakage risk, and breaks API consistency. Solution must propagate groups through _get_best_new_feature() to cross_val_score() while maintaining backward compatibility, enabling proper validation in healthcare, time-series, and multi-site ML scenarios.

Clarification questions regarding groups parameter implementation in SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(): splitter compatibility validation, error handling for unsupported splitters, backward compatibility strategy, internal propagation logic through _get_best_new_feature(), edge cases in group consistency, documentation requirements, and cv parameter validation interactions.

Clarification needed on groups parameter semantics: interaction with cv splitter types, error handling for incompatible splitters, backward compatibility requirements, validation strategy, and documentation scope for grouped cross-validation in SequentialFeatureSelector.

EndUser raises six clarification questions addressing groups parameter handling: splitter compatibility validation strategy, backward compatibility defaults, validation timing, complete propagation chain through internal methods, transform-time persistence, and API consistency with existing scikit-learn estimators. These questions resolve ambiguities in the proposed solution before implementation begins.

EndUser confirms groups parameter requirement with refinements: make it optional (default None) for backward compatibility, raise ValueError when cv splitter incompatible with groups, validate splitter's split() signature early, and document recommended splitter types for grouped data scenarios. This resolves pain points around grouped/hierarchical data validation while maintaining sklearn API consistency.

End user requirements validated and refined: groups parameter must be optional (default None) for backward compatibility, propagate through the fit→_get_best_new_feature→cross_val_score chain, and raise ValueError with clear messaging when incompatible with the cv splitter. This resolves the pain point of grouped/hierarchical data handling in healthcare ML pipelines and eliminates the need for custom wrapper code.

End user confirms groups parameter as optional (default None) for backward compatibility, validates propagation chain through fit/cross_val_score, and refines error handling to raise ValueError when groups incompatibility detected. Requirements address grouped/hierarchical data validation in healthcare and time-series contexts.

Consolidated 8 structured elicitation records documenting the SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter requirement. Records capture workflow context (grouped data validation), functional specification (groups parameter propagation chain), backward compatibility constraint (optional, default None), validation rule (explicit error on unsupported cv splitters), behavioral specification (sklearn conventions), use case validation (healthcare ML), design alignment (sklearn patterns), and implementation constraints (non-breaking change). All records grounded in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 documentation standards and validated against enduser confirmations and refinements.

Synthesized 7-item hierarchical requirement list (1 MUST functional, 1 MUST backward-compatibility, 1 MUST validation, 2 SHOULD behavioral, 2 COULD enhancement) for adding optional groups parameter to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() to enable group-based cross-validation on hierarchical/grouped datasets while maintaining API compatibility and preventing splitter-groups mismatches via explicit validation.

Targeted Deployer questions probe infrastructure constraints (deployment environments, version compatibility), security mandates (data validation, audit trails for groups parameter), scalability expectations (large hierarchical datasets, validation overhead), API stability (backward compatibility across sklearn versions), error handling infrastructure (logging/monitoring for ValueError scenarios), testing requirements (grouped dataset integration tests), and rollout strategy (feature flagging, user migration path). Questions decompose the groups parameter implementation into operational dimensions: where it runs, how it's secured, whether it scales, how it versioning, how failures are handled, how it's validated, and how it's released.

Chain-of-Thought reasoning: The Deployer must clarify infrastructure scale (grouped dataset characteristics), security posture (groups parameter validation timing and audit requirements), and scalability strategy (error handling distribution, type checking eagerness) to ensure the groups parameter implementation aligns with production deployment constraints. Key probe areas: deployment targets and backward compatibility timelines; grouped data scale and performance constraints; validation centralization vs. distribution; exception handling and observability patterns.

Seven targeted Interviewer questions probe deployment infrastructure constraints (version support, CI/CD integration), security/privacy mandates (group identifier handling), scalability expectations (dataset sizes, performance benchmarks), validation framework requirements (error handling patterns), integration complexity (Pipeline/GridSearchCV compatibility), rollout strategy (release timing, backward compatibility obligations), and observability needs (usage monitoring). Questions anchor to the groups parameter propagation chain and cv splitter compatibility validation already established in elicitation records.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for groups parameter implementation in SequentialFeatureSelector: validation logic via cv splitter introspection, type checking on groups input, backward-compatible default None, explicit error handling for incompatible splitters, linear scalability, and comprehensive test coverage. No new infrastructure required; deployment cost minimal.

Deploy groups parameter support in SequentialFeatureSelector through validated parameter propagation (fit→_get_best_new_feature→cross_val_score) with mandatory type/shape validation, cv splitter compatibility checking, optional parameter with None default for backward compatibility, and explicit error handling for incompatible splitter-groups combinations; CI/CD SHALL test across multiple cv splitter types with grouped datasets.

Deploy groups parameter support in SequentialFeatureSelector with mandatory input validation (type, shape, range), cv splitter introspection to detect group-support capability, explicit error handling with actionable messages, backward compatibility preservation (groups=None default), and O(n) scalability for large hierarchical datasets. CI/CD matrix testing across Python 3.8+ and scikit-learn 0.24+ with regression verification required pre-deployment.

Five clarifications requested on infrastructure validation mechanism for cv splitter introspection, security validation responsibility boundary, backward compatibility testing scope, error handling timing strategy, and groups parameter propagation semantics to resolve operational ambiguities before implementation.

Deployer RaiseQuestionDeployer identified five critical clarifications needed on infrastructure validation mechanism for cv splitter groups support detection, security validation scope and timing, minimum scikit-learn version requirements, error handling behavior specification, and performance interaction with SequentialFeatureSelector parameters. These clarifications are essential before implementation can proceed with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 compliance.

Six critical clarifications required from domain experts to resolve deployer infrastructure, security, and compatibility concerns: (1) exact scikit-learn version matrix and API stability for groups support, (2) authoritative mechanism for detecting cv splitter groups capability (hasattr, signature inspection, or test invocation), (3) timing and scope of groups validation in fit() vs _get_best_new_feature(), (4) error handling strategy alignment with scikit-learn conventions, (5) edge case handling for groups parameter types and values, (6) comprehensive CI/CD test matrix specifications. These clarifications are prerequisite to implementation and deployment.

Deployer confirms groups parameter implementation strategy: use inspect.signature() for cv splitter detection, validate shape/type in fit() before propagation, enforce minimum scikit-learn 0.24.0, raise explicit ValueError on incompatibility, maintain backward compatibility via None default, execute comprehensive CI/CD matrix testing across Python 3.8-3.11 and scikit-learn 0.24-1.3.x. All clarifications resolved; ready for development handoff.

Deployer confirms groups parameter implementation with inspect.signature()-based detection, immediate shape validation in fit(), scikit-learn 0.24+ minimum version, comprehensive CI/CD matrix testing, and explicit error handling for incompatible cv splitters. Backward compatibility maintained via None default. Security mandate enforced through type/shape/range validation before cross_val_score() propagation.

Deployer role confirms deployment readiness for groups parameter feature in SequentialFeatureSelector: introspection mechanism validated via inspect.signature(), shape validation positioned in fit() for fail-fast behavior, scikit-learn 0.24.0+ baseline enforced, security validation implemented, backward compatibility preserved via None default, and error messaging made explicit for incompatible splitter scenarios. All infrastructure, security, and scalability requirements satisfied; deployment can proceed to implementation phase.

Operating environment specifies Python 3.8+ with scikit-learn 0.24.0+ runtime, CI/CD matrix testing infrastructure, inspect-based cv splitter introspection, type/shape/value validation for groups parameter, support for GroupKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold splitters, ValueError exception handling for incompatible cv splitters, grouped data handling (time series, clinical trials, cohorts), backward compatibility baseline, and early validation in fit() method before internal propagation.

System requirements consolidated from user-level (groups parameter support for grouped cross-validation), environment-level (Python 3.8+, scikit-learn 0.24.0+), and quality attributes (backward compatibility, explicit validation, error handling). Eleven requirements span functional (parameter propagation), validation (splitter detection, shape checking), behavioral (cv splitter conventions), and operational (CI/CD matrix testing) domains aligned with IEEE 830 format and scikit-learn API consistency.

Selected UML Use Case Diagram as primary model to capture actor interactions (Data Scientists performing grouped feature selection) and system responses (parameter propagation, validation, error handling); complemented by SysML Block Definition and Internal Block Diagrams to model call chain architecture (fit → _get_best_new_feature → cross_val_score), cv splitter type discrimination logic, and validation checkpoints. This dual-model approach addresses functional requirements (SYS-REQ-001, SYS-REQ-002), validation requirements (SYS-REQ-003, SYS-REQ-004, SYS-REQ-005), and quality attributes (backward compatibility, robustness, maintainability) while satisfying IEEE 830 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 specification standards.

SRS exhibits moderate quality issues across ISO 29148 attributes: CLARITY defects in type specification ('array-like') and ambiguous handling directives; FEASIBILITY concerns regarding performance of runtime introspection; VERIFIABILITY gaps in type validation and timing acceptance criteria; TRACEABILITY breaks between SRS sections and elicitation records; CONSISTENCY conflicts on error-raising behavior requiring explicit user confirmation. Critical gap: type and value validation requirements identified in gap analysis but not formalized as system requirements. Recommend: (1) define array-like type precisely with dtype constraints, (2) formalize type/value validation as SYS-REQ-007/008, (3) add performance optimization guidance for splitter detection, (4) establish measurable acceptance criteria for validation timing, (5) cross-reference enduser confirmations in SRS conflict resolution sections.

All six review findings from SRS revision closure examination have been confirmed as resolved. Clarifications include: array-like type enumeration (list, tuple, ndarray, Series), negligible performance overhead for splitter detection, comprehensive type validation requirements, bidirectional traceability restoration, error message standardization, and TimeSeriesSplit incompatibility handling. SRS now satisfies ISO 29148 clarity, feasibility, verifiability, traceability, and consistency quality attributes. Closure confirmed; requirements ready for implementation phase.
